edits.find: The stem gives an elderly man with dysphagia, regurgitation of undigested food, halitosis, and a gurgling sound in the neck. That cluster is Zenker — a pulsion pouch through the weak posterior hypopharyngeal wall because the cricopharyngeus fails to relax. The question the exam scores is not the diagnosis but the sequence: barium esophagram first, because a blind endoscope or nasogastric tube can enter the pouch and perforate it.
edits.with: An elderly man with dysphagia, regurgitation of undigested food, halitosis, and a gurgling sound in the neck has a Zenker diverticulum: a pulsion pouch through the weak posterior hypopharyngeal wall because the cricopharyngeus fails to relax. Order a barium esophagram first; a blind endoscope or nasogastric tube can enter the pouch and perforate it.

edits.find: The miss is usually a reflex: dysphagia → endoscopy. Ask what the endoscope could hit before you order it. Once the pouch is shown, treatment is cricopharyngeal myotomy (with or without diverticulectomy); the tested complication is aspiration pneumonia.
edits.with: Once the esophagram shows the pouch, treatment is cricopharyngeal myotomy (with or without diverticulectomy). The main complication is aspiration pneumonia.

edits.find: Regurgitated undigested food means the food never reached the stomach — the pouch or a non-emptying esophagus is holding it. Undigested regurgitation plus a neck finding is the pouch; undigested regurgitation plus dysphagia to liquids from day one is achalasia. Either way the first study is the esophagram; endoscopy leads only when the stem carries an alarm feature for cancer (weight loss, smoking, progressive solid dysphagia) and no neck finding.
edits.with: Regurgitated undigested food never reached the stomach; a pouch or a non-emptying esophagus held it. With a neck finding it is a Zenker pouch; with dysphagia to liquids from day one it is achalasia. In both, the first study is the esophagram. Endoscopy comes first only with an alarm feature for cancer (weight loss, smoking, progressive solid dysphagia) and no neck finding.

edits.find: Zenker is a false (pulsion) diverticulum — mucosa and submucosa herniate through the posterior wall between the inferior pharyngeal constrictor and the cricopharyngeus · the mechanism tested is cricopharyngeal motor dysfunction, diminished relaxation, not a structural weakness alone · halitosis comes from food decaying in the pouch · the complication tested is aspiration pneumonia
edits.with: Zenker is a false (pulsion) diverticulum: mucosa and submucosa herniate through the posterior wall between the inferior pharyngeal constrictor and the cricopharyngeus · the mechanism is cricopharyngeal motor dysfunction (diminished relaxation), not structural weakness alone · halitosis comes from food decaying in the pouch · the main complication is aspiration pneumonia

edits.find: When the diagnosis implies a blind pouch or a cavity the instrument cannot see, image it before you instrument it — the esophagram before the endoscope in Zenker is the same rule as the ultrasound before the needle in a hip effusion.
edits.with: When the diagnosis implies a blind pouch or cavity the instrument cannot see, image it before instrumenting it: esophagram before endoscopy in Zenker, as with ultrasound before the needle in a hip effusion.

edits.find: Upper endoscopy is the right modality one step early — the blind scope can perforate the pouch the esophagram would have shown.
edits.with: Upper endoscopy is ordered too early; a blind scope can perforate the pouch that the esophagram would have shown.

edits.find: Weight loss and age pull toward cancer, but undigested regurgitation with a neck gurgle is the pouch, and the esophagram settles both.
edits.with: Weight loss and age suggest cancer, but undigested regurgitation with a neck gurgle indicates a pouch, and the esophagram evaluates both.

edits.find: Manometry is the right family of test for a motility cause, but it answers achalasia, not a pharyngeal pouch.
edits.with: Manometry evaluates motility disorders such as achalasia, not a pharyngeal pouch.

edits.find: Everything before the mouth reads as ordinary adolescent iron deficiency: a 13-year-old, six-day menses, microcytic anaemia. Then brown macules on the lips and buccal mucosa appear, and they are not part of that story. They are the mucocutaneous marker of Peutz-Jeghers syndrome, and the anaemia becomes occult bleeding from hamartomatous polyps rather than menstrual loss. The next step is upper and lower endoscopy.
edits.with: A 13-year-old with six-day menses and microcytic anaemia suggests menstrual iron deficiency, but brown macules on the lips and buccal mucosa are the mucocutaneous marker of Peutz-Jeghers syndrome. The anaemia is then occult bleeding from hamartomatous polyps, not menstrual loss. The next step is upper and lower endoscopy.

edits.find: This is a stem where the answer lives in one clause of the physical examination and every earlier sentence points the other way. The distractor that fits the demographic — iron and an oral contraceptive — treats the anaemia and leaves the syndrome undiagnosed.
edits.with: Iron and an oral contraceptive treat the anaemia but leave the syndrome undiagnosed.

edits.find: Microcytic anaemia in an adolescent girl is not automatically menstrual — look at the mouth, the palms and the family history before settling · Intussusception in an older child is a lead point until proven otherwise, and a hamartoma is one · Cancer risk extends beyond the gut to breast and genital tract, so surveillance is lifelong · A normal platelet and leukocyte count argues against marrow failure
edits.with: Microcytic anaemia in an adolescent girl is not automatically menstrual — check the mouth, palms and family history · Intussusception in an older child has a lead point until proven otherwise; a hamartoma can be one · Cancer risk includes breast and genital tract, so surveillance is lifelong · Normal platelet and leukocyte counts argue against marrow failure

edits.find: The macules can fade in adulthood while the polyp risk does not — a negative skin examination in a parent does not exclude the family history

edits.find: When a stem builds an ordinary explanation and then adds one finding that does not belong to it, that finding is the question — the preceding sentences were the distractor.
edits.with: When one finding does not fit an otherwise ordinary explanation, that finding usually determines the diagnosis.

edits.find: Adolescent girl plus menses plus microcytic anaemia reads as iron deficiency before the mouth is examined.

edits.find: The newborn breaks down fetal hemoglobin quickly while hepatic UDP-glucuronosyltransferase is still immature, so unconjugated bilirubin accumulates faster than it can be cleared. A well infant, feeding and voiding normally, jaundiced on day 4 at 11 mg/dL, is the ordinary version of this.
edits.with: The newborn breaks down fetal hemoglobin quickly while hepatic UDP-glucuronosyltransferase is still immature, so unconjugated bilirubin accumulates. A well infant, feeding and voiding normally, jaundiced on day 4 at 11 mg/dL has physiologic jaundice.

edits.find: Every wrong option on that list is a real mechanism stated in the wrong direction or the wrong compartment. Ligandin is low at birth, not high. Enterohepatic circulation is increased in the newborn, not decreased. Cholestasis produces a direct hyperbilirubinemia, which this infant does not have. Albumin displacement is real but needs a displacing drug. Name the direction before you pick the mechanism.
edits.with: Each wrong option is a real mechanism stated in the wrong direction or the wrong compartment. Ligandin is low at birth. Enterohepatic circulation is increased in the newborn. edits.find: Both ends have already been scoped and are clean, which moves the search to the small bowel — the segment neither scope reaches. In a child the commonest small-bowel bleeding lesion is a Meckel diverticulum, and the study that finds it is a technetium 99m pertechnetate scan, which images the ectopic gastric mucosa rather than the bleeding itself.
edits.with: Both ends have been scoped and are clean, so the source is in the small bowel, which neither scope reaches. edits.find: Age changes the answer at this exact fork. An adult with the same negative workup gets capsule endoscopy, because the adult small-bowel causes are angiodysplasia, neoplasia and ulcers. Same algorithm, different branch.
